subject: Sealed unwrap proxy — on‑prem VPC keyflow design & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@keysafe.io>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sealed unwrap proxy — on‑prem VPC keyflow design & next steps

Hi all,

Attached is a first pass on a sealed unwrap proxy pattern I sketched for BrightBank's private deployment. The goal: allow BrightBank to keep HSM‑protected KEKs (customer BYOK) on their VPC while letting our on‑prem inference nodes request ephemeral wrapped keys for model decryption without ever exposing plaintext KEKs to our workers.

Key elements:
- HSM (customer) holds root KEK; KeySafe agent on customer side performs wrapping/unwrapping attestations.
- Sealed unwrap proxy (S‑Proxy) runs in the customer VPC as a small, mutually authenticated service that accepts short lived unwrap requests from Redwood workers and returns an ephemeral DEK wrapped under a service KEK.
- Attestation chain: HW attestation from customer's HSM -> KeySafe attest token -> Redwood validates token against attestation policy (nonce + timestamp).
- Short rotation and ephemeral DEK TTL (default 1h). Auditable, KV logs forwarded to BrightBank's central logging.

Open items I want feedback on:
1) Attestation format: do we accept KeySafe JWT + HSM cert chain, or require a PKCS#7 style signed blob?
2) Operator responsibilities: who runs the S‑Proxy (customer or KeySafe) and what minimal privileges are required?
3) Rotation: suggested KEK rotation cadence and emergency unseal procedure for operator eviction.
4) Network flow: proposals for minimal egress (mTLS only on 443, pinned certs) vs allowing private crossconnect tunnels.

Attachments: sealed-proxy-diagram-v1.png (diagram/png), protocol-draft-v0.3.md (text) — both in Drive link below.

Please reply with short notes rather than long edits — we'll iterate and lock down for BrightBank's security review next week.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@keysafe.io>

Subject: Re: Sealed unwrap proxy — on‑prem VPC keyflow design & next steps

Thanks for the writeup, Rishi — good concise framing. A few quick clarifications from the KeySafe side: 

- Attestation format: we can emit a compact attestation token (signed JWT) that embeds HSM certificate fingerprints and an HSM‑signed nonce. We also support optional PKCS#7 bundles if BrightBank insists on that format. Our JWT includes an "attest_chain" claim with the HSM serial and firmware version.

- S‑Proxy operator: we recommend the proxy be deployed as a customer‑owned service inside the VPC (KeySafe provides the container and image). That keeps KEK firmly in customer control; KeySafe's role is image maintenance and optional remote attestation tooling.

- Privileges: the proxy needs only unwrap rights (Unwrap/Decrypt) scoped to a single KEK and a service TLS keypair for mTLS. No signing permissions required.

- Network: mTLS over port 8443 (internal) + optional transit via private peering. For customers that cannot open any egress, a short‑lived reverse‑proxy (customer -> Redwood control channel) can be considered, but that requires stronger auditing.

Questions for you / BrightBank team: 
1) Do you want the attestation tokens to include operator identity (e.g., KeySafe image hash + owner id) or strictly hardware evidence?
2) For rotation, is BrightBank comfortable with a 90‑day KEK rotation, with emergency rotate within 24h for operator eviction?

I'll attach a sample attestation payload (attestation-sample.json) to illustrate.

—Alex
Alex Taylor
Head of Integrations, KeySafe Solutions
alex.taylor@keysafe.io

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sealed unwrap proxy — on‑prem VPC keyflow design & next steps

Quick notes from infra/securityops POV: 

- Audit: we need both sides to ship unwrap logs to BrightBank's logging endpoint (Logstash/Fluent). Logs must include request nonce, token fingerprint, requesting Redwood node id, and DEK wrapping meta (no plaintext keys). Retention per BrightBank SLA (90 days).

- Rotation: agreed on 90d standard; require an emergency rotate path that can be triggered by BrightBank security and executed with RBAC and two human approvals (customer sec lead + Redwood CS lead). Document the emergency unseal script in the runbook.

- Operator eviction: if KeySafe image is compromised or operator key needs revocation, KeySafe must publish a revoke statement and BrightBank will rotate KEKs. We need a staging plan for zero‑downtime rewraps: run dual KEK windows for X hours while nodes scale.

- Network / minimal egress: prefer private peering for production; mTLS+pinning acceptable for pilots. If BrightBank requires no outbound, propose a pull model where S‑Proxy polls Redwood control plane for signed requests (pull interval <= 30s).

I'll inline a short checklist we should add to the runbook: 
1) Image signing policy + verification steps
2) Attestation verification TTL and clock sync checks
3) Log schema + fields for audit
4) Emergency KEK rotate playbook

Thanks — we should lock the runbook items in JIRA-RED-1012 and get BrightBank's SecOps on a call Friday.

—Monica

Subject: Re: Sealed unwrap proxy — on‑prem VPC keyflow design & next steps

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below.

Decisions (agreed):
- Deploy S‑Proxy as customer‑owned container (BrightBank runs in VPC). KeySafe supplies signed image and attestation tooling.
- Attestation token: KeySafe JWT with embedded HSM cert fingerprint + image hash. Redwood will accept JWTs and verify image hash against a pinned allowlist.
- Rotation: 90d KEK rotation, emergency rotate within 24h with two approvals. Dual KEK rewrap window supported.
- Network: prefer private peering for prod; mTLS (pinned certs) acceptable for pilot.
- Logs: unwrap events forwarded to BrightBank logging endpoint with required fields; retention 90d.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Alex (KeySafe): produce final attestation JWT schema + sample payloads. Attach: attestation-sample.json — ETA Tue 2026-08-24.
- Monica (Infra Sec): draft runbook section (image verification, attestation TTL, emergency rotate) in JIRA-RED-1012 — ETA Mon 2026-08-23.
- Karthik (Platform): add S‑Proxy client SDK support for unwrap/token validation; update worker config to cache ephemeral DEKs — ETA Wed 2026-08-26.
- Rishi (me): coordinate BrightBank secops call Friday 2026-08-28 and fold feedback into final package.

Attachments referenced: sealed-proxy-diagram-v1.png, protocol-draft-v0.3.md, attestation-sample.json. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleDriveLink/proposal-sealed-proxy

If no objections, I'll mark this design as "pilot approved" and send the package to BrightBank.

Best,
